reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens. The idea fails on ceiling, on transfer and on measurability. (1) CEILING FROM THE FORMULA. Public anchor (GUESS from r1_hyp_divisions.json): TP 19 / FP 13 / FN 21, J 0.3585, U 53. One evaluable event is worth: FP->TP flip +0.0026, dropped FP +0.0007, dropped TP -0.0019 (official micro-J x 0.1; scratchpad sim). The idea's +0.007 upper bound is arithmetically right (8 x (1.36 x 0.6 - 0.36)/50), but its input is wrong. Probe 35 inserts about 12 public forks, and only ~3% of insertions are evaluable (CONF: 15 of 466, r1_research_div-cap-private-j.json). That gives ~0.4-1.2 evaluable public forks, not 8. A beta/p_edge_min rerank at cap 4 does not raise the count; it only reorders or removes the same ~12. Monte Carlo over 12 insertions at base precision 0.27: with evaluable fraction 0.03, mean +0.0001 to +0.0004 and P(>= +0.002) 0.02-0.12; at 0.10, mean +0.0003 to +0.0013 and P 0.08-0.36. Reaching a +0.002 mean needs an evaluable fraction >= 0.3 AND in-sample-grade discrimination at the same time. (2) WHAT RE-PICKING v CAN FIX IS LIMITED. Of the 43 local FP forks, 15 have the ADDED child right and the ILP-side child wrong, so p_edge on the added daughter cannot fix them (r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.json). The true second daughter is in the orphan pool for only 58/151 divisions and in the steal pool for 97/151 (B32 reach audit, CONTEXT.md l.203). Also, final probs are softmax over SOURCES per target (x138 cell 4 dump hook; predict_unet_transformer.py l.457). An ILP-chosen w->v already holds p >= 0.48, so p(u->v) <= 0.52, and the steal rule 'p(u->v) > p(w->v) + margin' can rarely fire against a scored edge. It only discriminates against 0.0 relink edges, which the current steal rule already targets. (3) TRANSFER. The edge net is trained with BCE on annotated rows and columns of all 199 videos (r1_verify_oof-edge-scorer-full-candidates_transfer.json), so all 151 GT daughter edges were training targets. Lab p_edge on exactly the evaluable daughter pairs is memorised. This is the same trap as the edge filter: lab +0.016, LB 0 (#29/#30). Direct in-sample evidence that the edge net's pairwise evidence is a WEAK division signal: letting it create forks through the ILP (exp12, div weight 0.6, 48 videos, CONTEXT.md l.85) gave 24 TP / 103 FP. That is precision 0.19, below the public break-even of 0.265, on the old metric (probably worse on the official one). LB probe 3 (div 1.2 -> 0.9) was neutral. The insertion's edge side is already net-negative in-sample (+5 TP / +7 FP from steals and second-daughter edges). The linajea citation does not transfer to this mechanism: its FP-division cut 0.89 -> 0.11 comes from a NODE-level cell-state classifier used as ILP constraints on in-distribution data. That is the role DaughterNet already plays, not a pairwise edge score. DaughterNet's 'OOF' p is within-embryo, not by embryo. 44b6 is one recording (overlapping crops), so its lab events count about once. (4) MEASURABILITY. LB noise is ~0.003 (byte-identical twins 0.946/0.942), and the expected effect is <= 0.001. The idea's adoption rule 'a tie is acceptable' would therefore adopt noise. The lab gate (CONF >= +0.002) passes by chance about 25% of the time when the true effect is 0 (SE ~0.0017 per the sibling retune verdict), and in-sample it would pass even if out-of-sample were 0. (5) Node multiplier: node-identical, so neither an artefact nor a gain. (6) It is not new: v2 had the same arm (edge-net-second-daughter, merged into oof-edge-scorer-full-candidates), and all three verifiers refuted it.
fix_if_any: No version clears +0.002 public. The least-harmful repair: (a) Do NOT use p_edge_min as a filter. Dropping one public TP costs -0.0019, dropping one FP gains only +0.0007, and p_edge's in-sample calibration on daughter edges will not hold. (b) Use p_edge only as a WITHIN-PARENT TIE-BREAKER: for a fixed parent u already chosen by DaughterNet, pick argmax over candidate v of p_dau(v) x p_edge(u,v)^0.5. Keep the insertion count and cap identical to #35, so it cannot remove TPs. (c) Replace the steal gate by the transfer-safe rule 'steal only from 0.0 (unscored relink) edges whose geometry fails the sister-symmetry check'. (d) Lab gate on the x138 dump, counting 44b6 once per unique GT division: >= +2 net evaluable flips on 6bba, 0 new FP, adj_edge within 0.0003. Discount the lab delta to 0 by default. (e) Never spend a dedicated LB slot. Ride along only on a probe already going out, and prefer spending division effort on J-invariant fork REMOVAL (fork-midpoint >= 4 um: 11 FP / 0 TP locally), which needs no network confidence. Only an embryo-held-out edge net (not feasible by 29 Sep) would make the p_edge part honestly testable.
